name: rat

attributes.attribute: magical power for the Celts is uncertain
could see the future in the Cotswolds
a sign of death at sea

sources: Briggs, Katherine M. The Folklore of the Cotswolds. London: B. T. Batsford Ltd., 1974, 127.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The rat is an animal of British folklore. It is not sure if the Celts gave this beast magical power. A trace of that belief stayed in the Cotswolds of England. There the people held that rats could see the fate to come. Rats that quit a house pointed to death within the family. A rat in a sieve, or one that swam past a boat in Scotland, pointed to death at sea.

okr.objective: Rat is a small British beast with an omen kly of death.
key_results: British folklore treats the rat as a beast of omen.
Celts may not have first given the rat magic.
In the Cotswolds, rats could read the future.
A rat near a boat told of death at sea.
